items.title: 61428_Red Callender oral history interview
items.q: So Trummy Young and Dexter and I, and Ulysses Livingston, and Arthur Dennis... we all go to Honolulu.

ctx.x: That was all you stayed in that one...

Well, that wiped it out. No, I stayed. The rest of the guys came back. Trummy stayed until he went with Louis years later. So I stayed, and then I came back and I decided to go back; I went back and played with the symphony. I stayed with the symphony for about three years, and meanwhile I had my own band, working at Lai Yi Chai's, which was probably the hippest Chinese restaurant you ever saw, run by Japanese. Tats Matsuo was the owner of Lai Yi Chai's, and I formed a six-piece band, which I called the "Biggest…

items.title: 52300_Trummy Young oral history interview
items.q: Willie Smith, Nat Cole, myself, Red Callender, we all used to go out and play them for him to help him out.

ctx.x: A lot of good -- it's hard to sit right down and think of all of them, but there's so many good players up there. It was a fun thing, you know. And they had a lot of drummers, lot of piano players, lot of bass players. Ray Brown, Red Callender, Ted Galner, Milt Hinton, Major Holley. And what's the little young bass player around New York, plays real good.
